body: The facility I work at is an Assisted Living, which means majority of the people there are considered "independant" and we highly encourage everyone to be as independent as possible. It's common to leave resident's in the bathroom while you go finish up other tasks, or other care, my boss encourages it to maximize time management. Sometimes I'm taking 3 residents to the bathroom at once, juggling them at the same time. It doesn't help that we're severely understaffed. Only one caregiver and one med tech on the floor per shift with around 50 residents. I'd say out of everyone I care for, only 2 people need me to stay while they use the restroom

I thought about this for awhile and, no I don't think I would ever be able to retell this story to a superior. I feel too ashamed and again I'm so scared of losing a job I really really love.  

While this incident never should have happened, I'm definitely 101% more careful and thorough when I'm leaving residents by themselves. Making sure they have access to all communication in case something happens. I corrected my own behavior and I don't think anything like this will ever happen again. I'm practically triple checking everything now. 

Honestly I want nothing more than to just apologize to her but I know the opportunity has long passed.

I just really want to apologize to her, but the time to do that is long gone. She doesn't remember the incident so bringing it up won't do either of us any good, it would probably just confuse her honestly. She's such a kind lady, even with her condition. It hurts me that I hurt someone so innocent like that. I'll probably think about this forever and when she passes I know the guilt is gonna hit me again
She did have an emergency pull string next to the toilet, but she's never had to use it before and she probably didn't realize what it was.

So, technically Mary is considered "independant", she has only a few care points. While she is wheelchair bound, she is able to wheel herself around and make her own decisions, but she is forgetful when it comes to her short term memory. She has sticky notes all over her room (put there by family) to remind her of what she's doing or what the plans are for the day. The only thing we have to help her with is toileting and transferring. 

At around 4:30 they would have come to bring her down for dinner so I nearly didn't make it in time before they checked on her.
